front: What are the card values in blackjack?
back: 2–10 = face value. J/Q/K = 10. Ace = 1 or 11, whichever helps.
why: The ace's dual value is what makes 'soft' hands flexible.
stat: Ten-value cards are 31% of the deck — why 10s drive every decision.

why: Avoid 6:5 tables — they quietly raise the house edge.
stat: You're dealt a natural about 4.7% of hands — roughly 1 in 21.

back: A tie. You and the dealer have the same total. Your bet is returned.
why: No win, no loss — bet comes back.
stat: A push returns your bet — no edge either way.

back: Going over 21. You lose immediately, even if the dealer busts after.
why: Player busts first — that's the core house edge.
stat: The dealer busts about 28% of the time on average — but you bust first.

front: Hit vs Stand — what's the difference?
back: Hit = take another card. Stand = keep your total, end your turn.
why: Every decision is built from these two actions.
stat: Hit or stand is ~70% of all decisions you'll make.

back: Double your bet, take exactly one more card, then stand.
why: Used when one card likely wins — turns good spots into bigger wins.
stat: Doubling 11 vs a 6 returns +0.67/unit — nearly double the win.

back: On a pair, split into two hands with a second equal bet.
why: Turns one weak hand into two stronger starts when correct.
stat: Splitting correctly adds value on ~6 of the 10 pairs.

back: Give up the hand after the dealer checks for blackjack; lose half your bet.
why: Cuts losses on hands too weak to play out (e.g. 16 vs 10).
stat: Surrender caps any loss at -0.50/unit — better than playing out a -0.54 hand.

why: It's a side bet with a high house edge — a sucker bet, even with a strong hand.
stat: Insurance returns -7.7% per unit — a flat losing bet.

front: What does 'dealer stands on soft 17' (S17) mean?
back: Dealer must stand on any 17, including A+6. They never hit a 17.
why: S17 is better for the player than H17 — this deck assumes S17.
stat: S17 vs H17 is worth about 0.2% to you — always pick the S17 table.

front: How do you signal hit vs stand?
back: Hit = tap the table. Stand = wave your hand flat over the cards.
why: Hand signals keep it clear for the dealer and the cameras.
stat: Hand signals are required at ~100% of US tables — cameras need them.

back: Your standard bet size, sized to your session bankroll (often 1–2%).
why: Betting in units keeps you in the game and controls variance.
stat: Bet 1–2% of bankroll per hand to survive normal swings.

front: What's the rule on chasing losses?
back: Don't. Keep your unit flat. Set a stop-loss and walk when you hit it.
why: Chasing blows bankrolls faster than any bad hand.
stat: Flat betting cuts your risk of ruin by more than half vs chasing.

front: Does perfect basic strategy beat the house?
back: No — it minimizes the house edge to ~0.5%, but doesn't flip it.
why: Strategy makes you lose slower; only counting can shift the edge.
stat: Perfect basic strategy holds the house edge near 0.5%.

stat: Can't bust on the next card — hitting is free value.

stat: Hitting 15 busts 54%; vs a 10 you only win 23% by standing.

stat: vs a 7, your 18 already wins 63% — stand, don't break it up.

stat: Split aces: each gets one card at a 31% shot at a ten — huge upgrade from soft 12.

why: Feels like you should stand on 16 — you shouldn't. It's the worst spot in the game.
stat: Stand and you win 23% / lose 77%. Hit busts 62%. Surrender caps it at -0.50.

why: The foundation of counting — every card shifts the count.
stat: Hi-Lo balances to 0 across a full deck — equal +1 and -1 cards.

back: A deck rich in 10s and aces favors the player (more blackjacks, better doubles).
why: You bet big when the remaining deck is in your favor.
stat: A deck rich in tens/aces lifts blackjack frequency above the base 4.7%.

back: The running total of all Hi-Lo tags you've seen since the shuffle.
why: It's the raw signal before adjusting for cards left.
stat: Running count is the raw signal — accurate only after the true-count step.

front: How do you get the true count?
back: True count = running count ÷ decks remaining.
why: Normalizes the count so a +5 means the same with 1 deck left or 5.
stat: Dividing by decks left can swing a +6 running count to a +2 or +6 true.

front: How does the true count guide betting?
back: Bet the minimum at 0 or below. Raise your bet as the true count climbs.
why: You profit by having more money out when the edge is yours.
stat: A solid count + bet spread can flip the ~0.5% house edge to ~+1% player edge.

back: Take insurance when the true count is +3 or higher.
why: The single most valuable count-based deviation.
stat: Base insurance is -7.7%, but at true +3 it turns profitable.

back: Stand on 16 vs 10 when the true count is 0 or higher (otherwise hit/surrender).
why: A deck-rich count means more cards bust your 16 — stand.
stat: At a high count, more tens left raises your 16-bust risk past 62% — stand.

back: Stand on 12 vs 3 when the true count is +2 or higher.
why: High count tips a borderline hit into a stand.
stat: 12 vs 3 flips from hit to stand around true +2.

back: Stand on 15 vs 10 when the true count is +4 or higher.
why: Another bust-risk spot that flips at a high count.
stat: 15 vs 10 flips from hit/surrender to stand around true +4.

back: Watch a table without playing, then jump in only when the count goes positive.
why: Lets you skip the negative-count hands entirely.
stat: Back-counting lets you skip the ~50% of shoes that run negative.
